title: Four comparisons, and the types behind them

prereqs.why: Every line here is decided by what the operands are converted to before the comparison happens.

statement:
Say exactly what this prints.

Each line is a comparison between two values that look comparable. The
question in every case is what the operands are converted to *before* the
comparison runs, and `std::boolalpha` makes the answer readable.

The `short`s and the `signed char` are promoted; one of the others is not.
hints: Integral promotion happens first: anything smaller than `int` becomes an `int`, whatever its signedness was. That settles two of the four lines before the usual-arithmetic-conversions rule is reached at all.

When the two operands are the same rank and one is unsigned, the signed one is converted to unsigned. On this platform `int` and `unsigned int` are the same rank; `long long` and `unsigned int` are not.
